Given the equations involving the variables \(x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_7\):

\[
\begin{aligned}
x_1 + 4x_2 + 9x_3 + 16x_4 + 25x_5 + 36x_6 + 49x_7 &= 1, \\
4x_1 + 9x_2 + 16x_3 + 25x_4 + 36x_5 + 49x_6 + 64x_7 &= 12, \\
9x_1 + 16x_2 + 25x_3 + 36x_4 + 49x_5 + 64x_6 + 81x_7 &= 123,
\end{aligned}
\]

we need to find the value of \(16x_1 + 25x_2 + 36x_3 + 49x_4 + 64x_5 + 81x_6 + 100x_7\).

We recognize that each equation can be expressed as a quadratic function \(S(k)\) where \(k\) is the shift in the coefficients. Specifically, \(S(k) = \sum_{i=1}^7 (i + k - 1)^2 x_i\). This function can be written as \(S(k) = Ak^2 + Bk + C\).

Given the values:
\[
\begin{aligned}
S(1) &= 1, \\
S(2) &= 12, \\
S(3) &= 123,
\end{aligned}
\]

we set up the following system of equations:
\[
\begin{aligned}
A + B + C &= 1, \\
4A + 2B + C &= 12, \\
9A + 3B + C &= 123.
\end{aligned}
\]

Subtracting successive equations, we find:
\[
\begin{aligned}
3A + B &= 11, \\
5A + B &= 111.
\end{aligned}
\]

Solving these, we get:
\[
\begin{aligned}
2A &= 100 \implies A = 50, \\
3(50) + B &= 11 \implies 150 + B = 11 \implies B = -139, \\
50 - 139 + C &= 1 \implies C = 90.
\end{aligned}
\]

Thus, \(S(k) = 50k^2 - 139k + 90\). To find \(S(4)\):
\[
S(4) = 50(4^2) - 139(4) + 90 = 50 \cdot 16 - 139 \cdot 4 + 90 = 800 - 556 + 90 = 334.
\]

Therefore, the value of \(16x_1 + 25x_2 + 36x_3 + 49x_4 + 64x_5 + 81x_6 + 100x_7\) is \(\boxed{334}\).
